title: Goroutine leaks: how they happen and how to avoid them

videos.script: A goroutine ends one way only. It returns. Nothing outside can stop it. So a goroutine that waits forever stays forever. {{first}} You start with a program that asks three servers and keeps the fastest answer. The answer is right. And after a hundred calls, two hundred goroutines are still waiting to send it. {{early}} Then a quieter leak. An error check returns early and skips the line that closes a channel. One goroutine left behind per error. {{find}} Next you ask the runtime where they are. A count, a profile that names the line, and a newer profile that lists only goroutines it can prove are stuck. You also see where that proof stops. {{fix}} Last, the fixes. Room in a buffer, a close that runs on every path, and a signal to stop. Before every go statement, three questions. {{close}} Lesson 7 limits concurrency on purpose, with a worker pool.
